simple.meaning: שׇׂכְלְתָנוּ (soklᵉthânûw) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “intelligence.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:11. Its contexts include family, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שׇׂכְלְתָנוּ (H7924).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שׇׂכְלְתָנוּ (soklᵉthânûw) / H7924 is traced through Daniel 5:11, Daniel 5:12, Daniel 5:14 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: There is a man in your kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. The king Nebuchadnezzar your father, yes, the king, your father, made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;

timeline.evidenceText: There is a man in your kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him. The king Nebuchadnezzar your father, yes, the king, your father, made him master of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;

because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.”
I have heard of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light, understanding, and excellent wisdom are found in you.
